index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents an overview of a prompt-based recommendation system, denoted as \sys, which leverages user and item features along with positive and negative feedback to generate personalized prompt embeddings and optimize a shared model. The global layout is divided into two main regions: a large dashed rectangular area on the left representing the prompt generation and optimization module, and a vertical blue container on the right labeled 'Base Model (fixed)', which processes user and item IDs. The base model contains a 'User Tower' (light green rectangle) receiving User ID (green triangle) and an 'Item Encoder' (gray rectangle) receiving Item ID (gray circle). Outputs from both towers are fed into a 'Fusion' block (trapezoid), which combines them to produce a joint representation. This fused output is then split into two components, one feeding into a loss function labeled \mathcal{L}_{rec} (recommendation loss) and the other into \mathcal{L}_{pape} (popularity-aware prompt-enhanced loss). These losses, along with another loss \mathcal{L}_{pfpe} (pinnacle feedback prompt-enhance loss), are used to train the system.

Within the left dashed region, the core of the prompt-based mechanism is shown. At the bottom, 'Neg Feedback' (green triangles) and 'Pos Feedback' (green triangles) are processed by a central 'Prompt Generator' (orange rounded rectangle). The Prompt Generator outputs prompt embeddings, which are then passed to two separate 'Embedding Encoder' blocks (light green rounded rectangles), one for each feedback type. Each encoder takes multiple input tokens (represented as small green rectangles) and produces a sequence of encoded representations (light green rectangles). These sequences are fed into two identical tower structures, each consisting of two layers: a lower layer with blue diagonal stripes and an upper layer with yellow diagonal stripes. These towers share model parameters, as indicated by the label 'Shared Model Parameter' connecting them. The outputs of these towers are pooled using 'Sum pooling' (gray rectangles with three segments), producing a final representation for each feedback type. The prompt embeddings from the Prompt Generator also feed directly into the towers, acting as a shared parameter. The outputs of the two sum-pooling operations are connected to the loss \mathcal{L}_{pfpe}, which is used to optimize the prompt generator and eliminate model bias. Additionally, the outputs of the towers are sent to the Fusion block in the base model, contributing to the final recommendation loss and popularity-aware loss. The entire system is designed to learn personalized prompts from user feedback to improve recommendation performance while mitigating bias through specialized loss functions.
